text:
The Canucks are 6-18-1, and our playoff odds have rounded to zero. Take the small joys where they come. On Saturday Marco Rossi scored twice against his former team, won 12 of 16 faceoffs, and Vancouver beat a Minnesota side that had gone 11-0-3 in its previous 14, in a shootout, with Leevi Meriläinen making big saves in overtime. A week earlier Filip Chytil's two goals ended a seven-game losing streak.

The bigger story is Elias Pettersson. He is on injured reserve with an upper-body injury, and his name is all over the trade market, with Elliotte Friedman among those reporting new turns. Brock Boeser, meanwhile, is being written about as the leader of this group, with some making the case for the C. It's Manny Malhotra's first season behind the bench, promoted from the AHL after Adam Foote's firing, and this is the roster he's been handed.

The numbers are as hard as the record. Vancouver has 39% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and 40% at 5v5, and it allows 3.92 expected goals per 60. The goaltending has made it worse: about nine more goals allowed than the chances against predict, and Kevin Lankinen at .802 and 9.3 goals worse than expected over his last five starts (0-5-0). The top pair of Filip Hronek and Zeev Buium gets only 32% of the expected goals.

What we'd watch: Buium's minutes, Rossi's role, and the phone lines.
